uncited: Sparse Voxel Storage and Management addresses the inefficiency of storing and rendering volumetric data where the majority of the space is empty or uniform.
By organizing voxels into hierarchical structures or compressed buffers, it reduces memory bandwidth and storage costs compared to dense grid representations [S1].

This family is distinct from [Naive Voxel Rendering](1103-naive-voxel-rendering.md) and [Instancing with Procedural/Shader Generation](2794-instancing-with-procedural-shader-generation.md) because it explicitly manages the data layout and hierarchy of the voxel primitives to optimize traversal and rendering, rather than relying on brute-force iteration or simple geometric instancing of all occupied cells.
**Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel is represented by one or more geometric primitives.
**Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space.
**Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized.
**Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view.
Sparse voxel techniques have evolved from early volume rendering methods that struggled with the memory requirements of dense 3D textures.

The specific techniques listed here, such as intensity-based storage and SVO LOD management, emerged from the need to optimize real-time rendering of these structures on modern GPUs, particularly in the context of neural radiance fields (NeRFs) and large-scale scientific visualization [S1][S2].
